sections.html:
You will find the Lincoln County Recorder of Deeds inside the courthouse at 201 Main Street, Troy, Missouri 63379. The office has a chief deputy clerk and two deputy clerks who handle the counter. For fee questions, call 636-528-0325.

Anything handed over after 3:30 pm waits until the next business day. With a late-afternoon closing, find out from the title company when the deed actually gets to Troy, because that decides the recording date.

Clerks check each paper against the recording statutes and stop there. Legal advice, title or lien searches, typing up a deed, blank forms, ownership disputes and notary work are all outside what they do. Take those to an attorney or your title agent. If you visit in person, bring your closing paperwork, and phone ahead when you are unsure whether a document counts as standard or non-standard, since the fee differs.

sections.h2: What the recorder keeps on file
sections.html:
This office is the county's home for land records and marriage licenses. Common filings include deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, surveys, plats, restrictions, wills, affidavits, patents and road rights of way. Servicemen's records are kept here too, and a tax lien goes on file when requested.

Filing is not a formality. RSMo 442.380: any written paper that transfers land goes to the recorder in the county where that land lies. RSMo 442.400: a deed that is never filed holds up only against the signers and people who knew about it. A buyer in that spot can face later claims, so get the deed to Troy within days of signing.

sections.h2: What does Lincoln County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Expect $26.00 for page one of a standard real estate document, then $3.00 per added page. Senate Bill 938 added $2.00 to the first-page fee, and $26.00 is the number to budget.

The statutory base is lower. RSMo 59.310 names $5 for page one and $3 for later pages. What you pay is the county schedule below, and the title company will show it on the settlement statement.

Lincoln County recorder fee schedule
Document or serviceCharge
Standard real estate document, first page$26.00
Each added page$3.00
Non-standard document, first page$49.00
Each added referenced release or assignment$5.00
Photocopy, letter, legal or ledger size$1.00 per page
Plat or larger survey copy$5.00 per page
Emailed document$1.00 per page plus a $2.00 email fee
Plat, 18 by 24 inches$46.00 plus $25.00 per added page
Survey, 18 by 24 inches$26.00 plus $5.00 per added page

Emailed copies must be paid by credit card, and the bank adds its own $2.00 charge.

sections.h2: Formatting rules that get a deed rejected
sections.html:
A deed that misses the layout rules comes back unrecorded, and that can delay your sale proceeds. The county checklist and RSMo 59.310 call for the following:

  • Leave 3 inches blank at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp.
  • Keep three-quarters of an inch of white space down both sides and along the bottom.
  • A legible legal description of the parcel.
  • A proper notarization, with the notary's signature legible and the seal placed legibly beneath it.
  • No handwritten documents.
  • Print in dark ink on light paper, with letters no smaller than eight-point.

The same section allows a recorder to take a nonconforming paper for an extra $25. Some papers are exempt, for example those signed before January 1, 2002 or executed outside the United States. Page one should carry the title, date, each grantor and marital status, each grantee, the addresses the statute calls for and the legal description. Your closing agent should build the deed around this list.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax bill after closing?
sections.html:
After recording, the transfer moves to the County Assessor, who changes the owner and mailing address on the tax file. The Lincoln County Collector describes the usual practice: seller and buyer divide the year's tax at closing, the seller's portion shows up as a credit to the buyer, and the buyer later pays the whole annual bill.

  • The assessor closes the files around August 31 so the collector can print the tax books. A name cannot be changed once the books are printed.
  • Got a bill in your name after the sale? Pull out your settlement sheet and have the collector confirm what was paid. The receipt covers the full year, and the sheet proves your share.
  • A wrong name or legal description in the assessor's file gets fixed with a corrected deed.
  • For closings after November 1, the closing agent typically pays the tax then, but an unpaid balance still follows the property to the new owner.

Missouri sends land with three years of unpaid tax to public auction. Lender foreclosure sales run under separate rules, and no courthouse posting is required for them.

Lincoln County sits in eastern Missouri on the Mississippi River and falls within the St. Louis metropolitan area. Population has risen fast, to an estimated 66,676 in July 2025. That is 11.9 percent above April 2020 and far above the 52,566 of 2010. Of 24,289 housing units, 79.0 percent are lived in by their owners, and the typical owner-occupied home is worth $244,300. Towns include Troy, Winfield, Moscow Mills, Old Monroe, Elsberry, Silex and Hawk Point.

sections.h2: From signing to the public record, step by step
sections.html:
1. Get the deed prepared by an attorney or title company, because the recorder will not type one.
  2. Sign in front of a notary and make sure the signature and seal can be read.
  3. Look over page one for the 3 inch blank top and the legal description.
  4. Pay the recording fee: $26.00 for page one, $3.00 for each page after.
  5. Get it to Troy before 3:30 pm for same-day recording.
  6. Check with the Assessor's office that ownership was updated.

Title companies do all of this routinely. Selling an inherited house? A small estate affidavit and certificate can be recorded to show the heirs hold title, so hand the probate papers to your closing agent early.

A little prep helps. Learn who will carry the deed to the counter and when, ask for the exact recording charge so it lands on the settlement statement, and save the recorded copy when it returns. A cash sale follows the same recording path. With no lender, there are usually fewer attachments, so the deed and its notary block are mostly what gets reviewed.

faqs.q: Does the Lincoln County recorder charge a transfer tax?
faqs.a: The fee schedule lists recording and copy charges and has no line for a transfer tax. Have the closing agent itemize each charge on your settlement statement, and call the recorder at 636-528-0325 if one looks unfamiliar.

faqs.q: What is the fee for page one of a deed?
faqs.a: Page one of a standard real estate document is $26.00, and every page after it is $3.00. A document the county classes as non-standard starts at $49.00 for page one.

faqs.q: Can the recorder help me write my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office reviews documents for recording requirements and does not draft deeds, hand out forms or search title. Hire a lawyer or a title agent.

faqs.q: What time must I deliver a document for same-day recording?
faqs.a: Before 3:30 pm. Anything presented later is recorded on the following business day.

faqs.q: Do I have to record a deed after selling my Lincoln County house?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sends every land conveyance to the recorder where the parcel sits, and an unrecorded deed binds only the parties and anyone with actual notice. Your closing agent normally files it.
